claim_statement: DistinctPartyPerBatch requires distinct modeled party identities across slots of one admitted batch.
allowed_statement: DistinctPartyPerBatch is the identity-level invariant whose necessity is analyzed.
limitation: Does not prohibit the same party across sessions, messages, or different batches.

claim_statement: R-semantics removes party-level admission and permits same-batch repeated-party composition.
allowed_statement: The relaxed model represents the absence of DistinctPartyPerBatch for the bounded comparison.
limitation: Bounded two-slot symbolic prototype; not a deployed-system claim.

claim_statement: Invalid repeated-party batch composition can yield two receiver accepts for one Send occurrence in the relaxed prototype.
allowed_statement: Duplicate receiver acceptance is reachable after removing party-level admission in the scoped model.
limitation: Does not by itself imply duplicate upper-layer consumption or installation.

claim_statement: P-semantics rejects same-party composition and restores intended batch identity semantics while retaining a reachable valid distinct-party batch.
allowed_statement: Party admission restores the intended batch identity semantics in the bounded abstraction.
limitation: Does not claim party admission is uniquely necessary for occurrence injectivity.

claim_statement: M-semantics rejects exact-message repetition but still permits two different messages from the same party in one batch.
allowed_statement: Message deduplication is an auxiliary comparison and does not enforce DistinctPartyPerBatch.
limitation: Message identity and scoped occurrence injectivity are not party-level batch identity semantics.

claim_statement: Duplicate receiver acceptance may extend to duplicate consumption or installation only through an explicit upper-layer composition boundary.
allowed_statement: Upper-layer impact remains conditional on a stated interface such as C_install-v2.
limitation: No unconditional or deployed upper-layer impact claim.
